  - region "Simple English explanation of Rationalisation":
    - paragraph: In simple English
    - heading "Understand Rationalisation" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "Rationalisation multiplies by a form of 1 so the denominator has no surd. 1/√2 = √2/2, 3/√5 = 3√5/5, and 1/(√3−1) = (√3+1)/2. A useful rule is Rationalising step: 1/sqrt(a) = sqrt(a)/a. You can learn Rationalisation by trying one small example instead of long theory."
    - paragraph: "Multiply numerator and denominator by the surd or the conjugate, then simplify the new denominator. Example: Rationalise 1/sqrt(2). Multiply by sqrt(2)/sqrt(2). The denominator becomes 2. So the answer is sqrt(2)/2."
    - paragraph: "In real life, exact slopes: Rationalised forms compare exact gradients. Watch out: Changing only the denominator. Multiply top and bottom by the same expression."
    - complementary:
      - generic: Try this example
      - paragraph: Rationalise 1/sqrt(2).
      - generic "Compare your answer"
